summary: New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people• Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research findsBritish businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.

stories.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
summary: Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm eventWith their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness.

A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads.On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs.

stories.title: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations
summary: The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards.

The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.
